name: Yatoke / Nakarhamto village wordlists
confidence_why: No source describes North Babar word stress: Taber (1993) and Edwards (2025) supply only wordlists whose stress marks fall mostly on the penultimate syllable (Edwards marks word-final long vowels as stressed, Taber marks many antepenults), and Blust (2013) and Steinhauer (2009) say nothing specific to this language, so any rule would be an inference from transcriptions rather than a documented pattern.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened both saved TSVs, 535 lines., 1516 lines). Every gloss+IPA pair in the quote is present verbatim at the cited line (Yatoke 29 enwuu [ɛnˈβuː], 39 oni [ˈɔ̝ni], 63 panyaa [panˈyaː], 82 kaʔ-o [ˈkaʔo], 161 udaa [uˈdaː], 194 wlenda [β̞lɛnˈdaː], 223 mede [ˈmɛdɛ̆], 285 ye-plii [yɛˈpliː], 445 ne-ʔinna [neˈʔinˑa], 474 me-prii [mɛˈpriː], 492 nitro [ˈniːtrɔ], 511 tatatn-a [taˈtaːtna], 530 anaraa [anaˈraː]; Nakarhamto 164 ewa-ni [ɛˈwːani], 167 ito [ˈitːɔ], 276 oti [ˈoti], 487 na-ape [ˈnaːpɛ], 708 dur-a [ˈduraʔ], 786 ayanna [ʔaˈyanːa], 1169 moror [mɔˈrɔr], 1235 ne-ʔni [nɛʔˈni], 1327 kaʔnan [kaʔˈnan], 1383 mawii [maˈβiː]). a full-text search for stress/accent the stress marks gives exactly 17 Yatoke…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for nort2860, so there is nothing to agree with or contradict. This work supplies the first stress evidence for North Babar, but only as IPA stress marks on 33 entries, not as a statement; it is data-level evidence for a penult default with heavy (long-vowel or closed) final syllables attracting stress. Consistent with the earlier tabulation of Taber's 1993 Nakarahamto list (ABVD id 309: 70 penult, 46 antepenult, 1 final of 121 stress-marked forms), whose antepenult cases mostly involve a final -ai/-ia/-ija/-ijɛ sequence counted here as two syllables. Two ELAR PDFs that may hold Edwards's transcription conventions and any stress statement…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The wordlists contain no statement about stress. Stress is marked in IPA on 17 Yatoke and 16 Nakarhamto entries only. In those 33 forms the mark falls on a final syllable whenever it has a long vowel (enˈβuː, uˈdaː, β̞lɛnˈdaː, panˈyaː, anaˈraː, yɛˈpliː, mɛˈpriː, maˈβiː, nɛpˈliˑ) and in Nakarhamto also on some final closed syllables (mɔˈrɔr, kaʔˈnan) and on a monosyllabic root after a prefix (ne-ʔni [nɛʔˈni]); otherwise it falls on the penult (ˈɔ̝ni, ˈkaʔo, ˈmɛdɛ̆, neˈʔinˑa, ˈniːtrɔ, taˈtaːtna, ˈitːɔ, ˈoti, ˈnaːpɛ, ˈduraʔ, ʔaˈyanːa, ɛˈwːani). This is my tabulation of transcription data, not a rule stated by the source; the closest fixed-list label is weight-sensitive (penult default, heavy final attracts stress).
new_statements.exceptions: none stated; the data include prefixed verbs where the mark sits on the root (ne-ʔni [nɛʔˈni], me-prii [mɛˈpriː], ye-plii [yɛˈpliː]) so the domain may be the root rather than the prefixed word; ede pe 'why?' [ɛdɛˈpɛˑ] and me-prii kromate [mɛˈpri krɔmaˈtɛː] are two-word phrases
new_statements.identity_note: The two wordlists describe two North Babar villages: Yatoke (BCD001, 480 items) and Nakarhamto (BCD007, 1500 items). Badan Bahasa's Peta Bahasa lists Yatoke and Pepra as the dialects of 'Bahasa Yatoke' (= North Babar). Both village lists show the same stress pattern in the marked forms.
